case_name: Randhir Singh v Union of India and Others
facts: Equal pay for equal work' is not a mere demagogic slogan.
The petitioner claims; so the petitioner asserts.
Art. 39(d) of the Constitution proclaims, as a Directive Principle, the Constitutional goal of 'equal pay for equal work for both men and women'.

Arts. 14 and 19 guarantee respectively the fundamental rights to equality before the law and equality of opportunity in the matter of public employment and Art. 32 provides the remedy for the enforcement of the fundamental rights.
The judges of the Court have a duty to redeem their Constitutional oath and do justice no less to the pavement dweller than to the guest of the five star hotel.
The scale of pay of a Driver-Constable in the Delhi Police Force is Rs. 210-270 in the case of nonmatriculates and Rs. 225-308 in the case of matriculates.
The scale of pay of drivers in the Railway Protection Force is Rs. 260-400.
The scale of pay of drivers in the office of the Language Commission is Rs. 260-350.
The pay scale of drivers of heavy vehicles in the Fire Brigade and the Department of Light House is Rs. 330-480.
issues: Is 'equal pay for equal work' a mere demagogic slogan?
Can the petitioner claim equal pay with other drivers in the Delhi Police Force?
Should the Pay Commission have considered the drivers as a separate category?
petitioner_arguments: The petitioner claims that he discharges the same duties as the rest of the drivers in the other offices; in fact he claims that he discharges more onerous duties than the others.

He complains that there is no reason whatsoever to discriminate against the petitioner and other driver Constables merely because he and his ilk happen to be described as constables as indeed they are bound to be so described, belonging as they do to the Police Force.
respondent_arguments: The respondents suggest that the petitioner was no more and no less than a constable of the Delhi Police Force and that there was no such category of Drivers in the Delhi Police Force.
It is submitted that there can be no comparison between the different departments of the Government of India for the purpose of fixation of pay scale.
court_reasoning: The principle, 'equal pay for equal work' is not an abstract doctrine but one of substance.

We cannot accept this view. If this view is to be stretched to its logical conclusion, the scales of pay of officers of the same rank in the Government of India may vary from department to department notwithstanding that their powers duties and responsibilities are identical.
holding: The Court holds that where all things are equal, persons holding identical posts may not be treated differentially in the matter of their pay merely because they belong to different departments.
The Court directs the respondents to give the petitioner his due, the same as they have given others like him.
